title: Holding Back Deductible Exposure on Overpayment Refunds — Insurance Claim Repairs Accounting Rule
content:
## Rule

While a supplement on an Insurance Claim Repairs repair order is undecided and part of the stated deductible is still unassessed, the deductible that supplement could still raise is held from an overpayment refund:

- the undecided supplement's full amount, when the unassessed deductible is at least that amount;
- the whole unassessed deductible, when it is smaller;
- nothing, when no supplement is undecided or no deductible is left unassessed.

The **unassessed deductible** is the deductible the insurer stated on the repair order less the deductible charges posted on it, never below zero. A supplement is **undecided** while the latest submitted supplement number is above the latest decided one; the undecided supplement's amount is the amount submitted on it.

The amount held is taken off the excess on the repair order before the refund is limited to the payment it returns; the refund never falls below zero.

## Input – judgement – output

| Supplement undecided | Unassessed deductible compared with its amount | Held |
|---|---|---|
| yes | at least the amount | the supplement's amount |
| yes | above zero but smaller than the amount | the whole unassessed deductible |
| yes | zero | nothing |
| no | any | nothing |

## Worked holds (hypothetical; stated deductible USD 1,000.00)

| Deductible charges posted | Unassessed | Undecided supplement amount | Held |
|---|---|---|---|
| USD 600.00 | USD 400.00 | USD 250.00 | USD 250.00 |
| USD 600.00 | USD 400.00 | USD 400.00 | USD 400.00 (at least the amount) |
| USD 600.00 | USD 400.00 | USD 900.00 | USD 400.00 |
| USD 1,000.00 | USD 0.00 | USD 900.00 | nothing |
| USD 600.00 | USD 400.00 | none undecided | nothing |
